itemListElement.name: How Much Does a Galápagos Trip Cost Per Day?

@graph.headline: How Much Does a Galápagos Trip Cost Per Day?

mainEntity.name: How much does a Galápagos trip cost per day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Roughly $150–$700 per person per day land-based (hotel plus day tours) or $445–$2,193 per day on a cruise, with a fleet median around $907. On top of either, everyone pays a one-off $200 park fee, a about $20 transit card and about $400–$500 in mainland flights.

mainEntity.name: Is a Galápagos cruise or a land-based trip cheaper per day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Land-based is cheaper day-for-day: $150–$700 versus $445–$2,193 on a cruise. The trade-off is reach — a land base gets you to about one-third of the visitor sites, while a 5-day-plus cruise can reach them all.

mainEntity.name: What is the Galápagos National Park entrance fee?

acceptedAnswer.text: $200 for most foreign adults, paid in cash on arrival. It rose on 1 August 2024 — the first increase since 1998. Children, Ecuadorians and CAN/MERCOSUR nationals pay reduced rates. It is a one-off gateway cost, not a daily one.

mainEntity.name: Are flights and park fees included in a Galápagos cruise price?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Mainland flights (about $400–$500), the $200 park fee and the about $20 INGALA transit card are extra on essentially every cruise fare, and so are international flights to Ecuador. Always budget these three fixed costs separately.

mainEntity.name: How much does a week in the Galápagos cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 7-day trip, plan roughly $2,070 budget land-based, $7,020 mid-range cruise (fleet median) or $11,170 high-end yacht per person — each figure includes the $200 park fee, about $20 card and about $450 flights. Your real total shifts with cabin, season and operator.

mainEntity.name: Does a more expensive cruise visit better islands?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Nearly all boats reach nearly all islands, so price buys the onboard experience — service, guiding, cuisine and cabins — not a better map. Every island is reachable on a 5-day-plus cruise; only Fernandina and west Isabela need more than a 4-day program.

mainEntity.name: What extra costs are not included on an all-inclusive Galápagos cruise?

acceptedAnswer.text: Beyond the fare: international flights to Ecuador, the about $400–$500 mainland hop, the $200 park fee, the about $20 transit card, travel insurance, crew tips, alcohol, wetsuit hire and any mainland hotel nights before or after the cruise. Budget these on top.

mainEntity.name: How can I do the Galápagos on a budget?

acceptedAnswer.text: Base yourself on land (about $150–$700/day), pick a shorter or lower-tier cruise (a 3-star cabin reaches the same headline islands), travel in the cool season or take a late cabin for price, share a cabin to dodge the solo supplement, and book flights separately.

mainEntity.name: Is there a solo traveller supplement in the Galápagos?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes — solo travellers can pay a single-occupancy premium on top of the per-day rate. It is not universal: some operators waive or reduce it on select departures, and sharing a cabin removes it entirely. Tell us your dates and we'll find the ones that don't penalise solo travellers.
